High Blood Pressure in a Child or Adolescent

device vs auscultation · adult cutoffs from age 13 · staging · recheck interval by stage · ambulatory monitoringHas auscultation confirmed the device reading, and what stage does the averaged value set?

Source vignette Pt – 17 yo M at a pre-participation examination for football; feels well; no illnesses, medications or family history; body mass index (BMI) 29; automated oscillometric reading 138/88 mm Hg, stated as the 95th percentile for age and height, then 140/89 mm Hg on the same device; rest of the examination normal · Q – the most appropriate next step in diagnosis; options spanned auscultatory measurement, echocardiography, 24-hour ambulatory monitoring and repeat device readings daily for 3 days or in 2 weeks

Bottom line
  • A high oscillometric reading is confirmed by auscultation at the same visit: at least two readings, averaged; the device reading is not staged.
  • From age 13, adult cutoffs apply: elevated 120 to 129 systolic with diastolic below 80; hypertension 130/80 or higher.
  • The averaged auscultatory stage sets the recheck interval; ambulatory monitoring confirms hypertension; lifestyle change comes first.
Who is screened
GroupHow often
Every child from age 3Yearly; an oscillometric device is acceptable for the screen
Obesity, kidney disease, coarctation or other aortic arch obstruction, diabetes, a drug that raises pressureAt every visit
5Diagnostic criteria
Categories, age 13 and older
CategoryAveraged auscultatory value
Elevated blood pressureSystolic 120 to 129 mm Hg with diastolic below 80
Stage 1 hypertension130/80 to 139/89 mm Hg
Stage 2 hypertension140/90 mm Hg or higher

Under age 13, the cutoffs are percentiles for age, height and sex: elevated at the 90th percentile, hypertension at the 95th.

What the category sets
CategoryNext
ElevatedAdvise lifestyle change; repeat auscultation at 6 months

8Follow-up
Once hypertension is confirmed
WhenDo
Persistently high readingsPressure in both arms seated and in a leg prone; the leg normally reads 10 to 20 mm Hg higher, so a leg lower than the arm suggests coarctation of the aorta
Every confirmed caseUrinalysis, electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and lipids; with obesity, screen for diabetes and fatty liver
First treatmentDASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet and physical activity of moderate to vigorous intensity, 30 to 60 minutes on at least 3 to 5 days each week
Drug therapy consideredEchocardiography for left ventricular hypertrophy
Symptoms, stage 2 without a modifiable cause, left ventricular hypertrophy, kidney disease or diabetes, or lifestyle failureStart a drug: ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor, angiotensin receptor blocker, calcium channel blocker or thiazide; beta blockers are not first line
Goal from age 13Below 130/80 mm Hg
Goal under age 13Below the 90th percentile for age, height and sex
Pause point
Obese adolescent with hypertension and a normal examination Offered: an extensive search for a secondary cause Most childhood hypertension is now primary → Baseline tests and lifestyle change; a secondary cause is sought only when the history or examination suggests one
Practice
  1. 17 yo M at a football pre-participation examination, well, BMI 29, automated oscillometric blood pressure 138/88 mm Hg and 140/89 mm Hg on repeat with the same device, otherwise normal examination → Blood pressure measurement by auscultation → the averaged auscultatory readings set the stage
  2. 15 yo F at a well visit with an automated reading of 136/82 mm Hg; two auscultatory readings at the same visit average 132/78 mm Hg → Stage 1 hypertension → a systolic of 130 to 139 mm Hg sets stage 1 even with a diastolic below 80
  3. 14 yo M at a well visit whose auscultatory readings average 124/76 mm Hg, with a normal examination → Lifestyle advice and recheck in 6 months → elevated blood pressure
  4. 16 yo F with obesity whose auscultatory averages are 134/84, 132/82 and 136/86 mm Hg at three visits over 3 months → 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring → confirms hypertension before workup and treatment
  5. 17 yo M, asymptomatic with a normal examination, whose auscultatory readings at one visit average 146/94 mm Hg → Lifestyle advice and referral within 1 week → stage 2 hypertension
  6. 16 yo M with obesity and hypertension confirmed by ambulatory monitoring whose blood pressure stays high after a trial of diet and exercise, so drug therapy is planned → Echocardiography → measures left ventricular mass before drug therapy
Guideline history The 2017 AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) guideline set fixed adult cutoffs from age 13 and kept percentiles only for children under 13. Under 13, hypertension starts at the 95th percentile for age, height and sex. From age 13, stage 1 starts at 130/80 mm Hg regardless of percentile.
Exit ramps Symptoms such as headache or cognitive change call for drug therapy (step 8) · Persistently high readings call for both arms seated and a leg prone; the leg normally reads higher, so a leg lower than the arm suggests coarctation of the aorta · Confirmed hypertension: baseline tests (step 8); a wider search for a secondary cause only when the history or examination points to one
Pearls Echocardiography is the test for cardiac damage once drug therapy is considered · Lifestyle change aimed at obesity is the first treatment for most adolescent hypertension · How NBME framed it: with the device reading already repeated, the key is a measurement method, not a diagnosis, heart test or later recheck
Pairs with Hypertension in an Adult covers confirmation, baseline tests, the secondary causes to test for, and drug choice in adults.
Transferable rule A high blood pressure from an automated device is confirmed by averaged auscultatory readings before it is staged, monitored, imaged or treated.
Sequencing trapEchocardiography looks for left ventricular hypertrophy once drug therapy is considered, and this reading is not yet confirmed.
Sequencing trapAmbulatory monitoring is accurate, but it follows auscultatory office readings that stay elevated for 1 year or in stage 1 across 3 visits.
Unchecked attributeDaily device readings for 3 days repeat the same overestimate; the method must change, not the number of readings.
True-fact-wrong-slotA 1 to 2 week recheck follows stage 1 confirmed by auscultation, but a repeat device reading in 2 weeks confirms nothing.
